SOURCE: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/harness-security.html
FETCHED: 2026-09-24 (first audit — carried debt from 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-23 reports)

SECURITY PRIMITIVES
- Isolated execution: every session in its own Firecracker microVM in AgentCore Runtime.
  No shared state, no shared filesystem.
- IAM execution role assumed by the harness; trust policy principal bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com
- Inbound OAuth (custom JWT authorizer) OR SigV4 (AWS IAM, default).
- VPC mode available; Cedar-based AgentCore Policy on Gateway gates tool calls.

*** SigV4 DOES NOT PROPAGATE PER-USER IDENTITY DOWNSTREAM. ***
Token Vault user-scoped OAuth storage and on-behalf-of token exchange are available ONLY
when the caller authenticates with a Bearer JWT via the OAuth inbound path. SigV4 support
for per-user identity is "planned for a future release."

TRUST BOUNDARY
"Any principal that passes the IAM or JWT authentication and authorization gate has access
to the full microVM session, including the tools and capabilities configured on the harness.
The harness validates the structure of the request it accepts, but it does not inspect the
meaning of prompts, screen content, or enforce behavioral constraints on the agent."
- Harness REJECTS toolUse blocks in the final InvokeHarness message (server-side), for both
  built-in server-side tools and inline functions.
- Non-harness AgentCore Runtime provides NO server-side protection — the agent entrypoint
  must strip toolUse blocks itself.
- toolResult IS accepted in the final message; inline-function handoffs resume via the same
  runtimeSessionId.

*** MODEL CONFIGURATION PARAMETERS — UNVALIDATED PASSTHROUGH ***
"The harness does not validate, filter, or restrict these parameters."
Callers who can set additionalParams can:
- Redirect requests to arbitrary endpoints — LiteLLM aws_bedrock_runtime_endpoint overrides
  the Bedrock endpoint URL; the SIGNED request INCLUDING THE SigV4 SIGNATURE AND SESSION
  CREDENTIALS is routed to the specified endpoint.
- Override HTTP headers — OpenAI extra_headers injects/overrides outbound headers INCLUDING
  Authorization.
- Attempt IAM role assumption — LiteLLM aws_role_name; succeeds or fails on the execution
  role's sts:AssumeRole permission.
- Change target model or region — modelId and apiBase redirect inference to a different
  model, region, or provider entirely.
Suggested mitigations (customer-side): strip/allowlist the `model` field, validate or remove
additionalParams/apiBase/modelId, deny sts:AssumeRole, scope network via VPC security groups.

*** SKILLS AND INSTRUCTIONS — TRUSTED-INPUT BY DESIGN ***
Skills = bundles of markdown and scripts fetched from Amazon S3 or Git AT INVOCATION TIME and
injected into the agent's context. "The harness treats all skill content as trusted input. It
does not validate, sanitize, or inspect the content or source of skills."
Skills can be OVERRIDDEN PER InvokeHarness CALL — a caller can supply their own skill sources
containing arbitrary instructions or scripts. Mitigations: strip the `skills` field,
allowlist S3 prefixes / Git repos.

OBSERVABILITY
Correlation identifiers propagate to Gateway, Memory, Code Interpreter, Browser for unified
CloudWatch traces. "These identifiers are used for observability only - they are never used
for authorization or data access decisions."

*** PAIRED IAM PERMISSION MODEL (14 harness APIs) ***
API                        -> Required IAM actions
InvokeHarness              -> InvokeHarness + InvokeAgentRuntime
InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand  -> InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand + InvokeAgentRuntime
InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell -> InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell
CreateHarness              -> CreateHarness + CreateAgentRuntime + CreateMemory
UpdateHarness              -> UpdateHarness + UpdateAgentRuntime + UpdateMemory
DeleteHarness              -> DeleteHarness + DeleteAgentRuntime + DeleteMemory
GetHarness                 -> GetHarness
ListHarnesses              -> ListHarnesses
CreateHarnessEndpoint      -> CreateHarnessEndpoint + CreateAgentRuntimeEndpoint
UpdateHarnessEndpoint      -> UpdateHarnessEndpoint + UpdateAgentRuntimeEndpoint
DeleteHarnessEndpoint      -> DeleteHarnessEndpoint + DeleteAgentRuntimeEndpoint
GetHarnessEndpoint         -> GetHarnessEndpoint
ListHarnessEndpoints       -> ListHarnessEndpoints
ListHarnessVersions        -> ListHarnessVersions

RESOURCE ARNS:
  arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:<region>:<accountId>:harness/<id>
  arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:<region>:<accountId>:harness/<id>/harness-endpoint/<endpointName>
Get/Update/DeleteHarnessEndpoint require BOTH ARNs. CreateHarnessEndpoint requires only the
harness ARN. Invoking a custom endpoint makes InvokeHarness and InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand
require both ARNs.

EXECUTION-ROLE REACH (sample policy + optional add-ons):
  bedrock:InvokeModel / InvokeModelWithResponseStream on foundation-model/* (all regions)
  ecr-public:GetAuthorizationToken, sts:GetServiceBearerToken
  xray:PutTraceSegments / PutTelemetryRecords / GetSamplingRules / GetSamplingTargets
  logs:CreateLogGroup / DescribeLogStreams / DescribeLogGroups / CreateLogStream /
    PutLogEvents / PutResourcePolicy(*)
  cloudwatch:PutMetricData (namespace bedrock-agentcore)
  bedrock-agentcore:GetWorkloadAccessToken, GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT
  Browser: StartBrowserSession, StopBrowserSession, GetBrowserSession, ListBrowserSessions,
    UpdateBrowserStream, ConnectBrowserAutomationStream, ConnectBrowserLiveViewStream
  Code Interpreter: Start/Stop/Get/ListCodeInterpreterSession(s), InvokeCodeInterpreter
  Memory: CreateEvent, DeleteEvent, GetEvent, ListEvents, RetrieveMemoryRecords
  Optional: lambda:InvokeFunction / sns:Publish / events:PutEvents (lifecycle hook targets);
    ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer / BatchGetImage / BatchCheckLayerAvailability (custom + VPC
    managed image pull from repository/harness-*); s3:GetObject + s3:ListBucket (skill
    sources); bedrock-agentcore:GetResourceApiKey + secretsmanager:GetSecretValue
    (bedrock-agentcore-identity!default/apikey/*); bedrock-agentcore:GetResourceOauth2Token
    + secretsmanager:GetSecretValue (.../oauth2/*); bedrock-agentcore:InvokeGateway

NETWORK: default = public network. VPC mode requires interface endpoints for ecr.dkr and
ecr.api, a gateway endpoint for s3, and bedrock-runtime if calling Bedrock. In VPC mode the
managed application container is pulled from a PRIVATE ECR repo named harness-<region> owned
by an AWS service account (ARN account wildcarded).

SHARED RESPONSIBILITY — customer owns: agent code security, IAM access controls, security of
commands executed in runtime sessions, session-to-user mapping enforcement, input validation
and PROMPT INJECTION PREVENTION, model configuration validation, skill and instruction
sources, container image updates, network configuration.

STILL UNAUDITED harness subpages: harness-skills, harness-memory, harness-environment,
harness-versioning, harness-export, harness-operations.
